body:
Concentration-round first-touch: promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, **Bug**, `domain:services` (lands in `service-datasource`'s `generateObjectDraft`). The platform's own validator refusing the platform's own generated output is a Bug on the review-before-commit flow, not polish. Scope: namespace prefix derivation + explicit `sharingModel` per the acceptance rules already settled for scaffolds (#9666's resolution is the precedent); acceptance = a generated draft passes `os build` out of the box, pinned.

Family coordination for the services seat: same generator as decision-box #10676 (PK seam) and #11000 (primaryKey emission — recommendation there is to STOP emitting the invalid key, which would remove a third `os build` failure from this same output). This card is dispatchable now (its two failures are independent of those rulings), but the five-gate fold test and a shared worktree are worth answering at claim if the rulings land first.

- Clause-②: **no** — this makes generated scaffold output valid where it was invalid. It adds no public surface and changes no accept/reject set. ⚠️ **But the object NAME changes** (`customers` → `${namespace}_customers`). If you find any consumer depending on the unprefixed name, that reading is wrong — stop and report.
- serial constraint: `packages/services/service-datasource/src/external-datasource-service.ts` (`generateObjectDraft` / `renderObjectSource`). **Free** — PR #11001 (#10676's catalog half) merged; it touched `refreshCatalog`, not the generator.

## Inherit the instrument the #10676 seat left you

That seat worked the same file and left a note worth more than the card's own fix direction:

> `renderObjectSource` annotates its output `ServiceObject`, so `tsc` over the rendered file is a cheap and **complete** acceptance instrument for that card — it caught this defect immediately.

Use it. Reproduce both failures on the current tree **before** fixing — the card measured at `79ebb37` and the tree has moved several times today. If either no longer reproduces, say so and stop.

## ⚠️ The acceptance boundary — read this before you write `Fixes`

The #10676 seat's other note is the one that decides how this card closes:

> Whoever takes #10712 should treat "the draft compiles and passes `os build`" as **one acceptance criterion spanning #10712 + #11000**, rather than two, or the card will be closed with the draft still not building.

**#11000** is a third defect in the same generator: `fields.FIELDNAME.primaryKey` is **not an authorable spec field key** — the rendered draft fails `tsc` with `TS2353` against the `ServiceObject` annotation the generator itself writes, and `ObjectSchema.safeParse` rejects it with `unrecognized_keys`. It is reachable today through the `opts.primaryKey` path, which the existing suite pins. Its routing is **blocked on a maintainer decision** on #10676.

So:

- Fix the two defects this card names (namespace prefix, `sharingModel`).
- Then **measure whether the draft actually passes `os build` end-to-end**, and say so explicitly for **both** cases: with `opts.primaryKey` unset (the default path) and with it set (the #11000 path).
- Use **`Fixes #10712`** only if this card's own two defects are discharged **and** you state plainly what the #11000 path still does. If the honest answer is "the default draft now builds; the `opts.primaryKey` path still does not, pending #11000", that is the right report — and it is `Fixes #10712` with that stated, not `Part of`, because #11000 is a separate card.

⛔ Do **not** fix #11000 here. Its resolution is a contract question the maintainer has not ruled.

## The `sharingModel` half — follow the precedent, do not invent

The card names the precedent: `security-owd-unset` is the same rule family #9666 hit for the app template, and #9666 has a **resolution**. Read it and follow whichever shape it prescribes for generated scaffolds — an explicit value, or the field emitted with a loud TODO the validator accepts. ⛔ Do not pick a default `sharingModel` on your own judgement: that is a security posture for every federated object this generator ever emits.

If #9666's resolution does not transfer, report `needs_decision` with what you measured rather than choosing.

## The namespace half

Derive the prefix from the datasource/package context. ⚠️ Say **where** you derived it from and what happens when that context is absent or empty — a generator that emits `_customers` on a missing namespace has traded one invalid draft for another.

## What must be pinned — both directions

- a generated draft **passes** `os build` (or the `tsc`-over-rendered-source instrument, whichever you can drive; say which and why).
- ⚠️ **still-generates (load-bearing)**: the draft still contains the introspected fields, the object still names the right remote table, and the `external` binding is intact. An implementation that emitted a minimal valid stub would pass a validator-only suite while destroying the thing the generator is for.
- both defects pinned **separately** — a single "it builds now" assertion cannot tell you which of the two you fixed, and cannot fail informatively when one regresses.
- the missing/empty-namespace case does something defensible, asserted.

## Standing proof standard

Ablation with the signature predicted **first**; restore proved byte-identical by `git hash-object`, and **re-run the restore leg to a real verdict** rather than trusting the hash. Prove `src/` vs `dist/` resolution argued from the files — ⚠️ #11001's seat measured `service-datasource` as having **no `dist/`** in its worktree, but the card says the defect was "confirmed in the shipped `dist`"; **re-verify rather than inheriting either claim**. Zero-hit counter-check with the **positive control run FIRST**. Gate union derived on the **final** commit, clean tree, `dispatch-gates.mjs` with **no path arguments**, exit codes captured before any pipe. Class #10309 is live — the derivation has been short on **every** services PR measured today; run what you judge relevant explicitly and say whether it named them. Changeset required. Draft PR only.

⚠️ A gate's refusal (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET` / `Nothing was checked` / `--re-measure cannot run`) is **NOT MEASURED**, never a pass — build the closure and re-run. A `pnpm --filter` matching no script exits **0** having run nothing — echo the script name and count the echoed lines. Never `git stash` (shared stack). Never report a grep hit count as a fact count.

⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/**` or `packages/spec` — zero ownership in this lane (note that #11000's likely fix *is* spec surface, which is another reason it is not yours).

## Refs

#10676 / PR #11001 (same generator, merged catalog half — read its body for the instrument and the notes) · **#11000** (the unauthorable `primaryKey` key — the acceptance boundary above) · #9666 (the `security-owd-unset` precedent) · #10675 (the CLI envelope card, which explicitly excludes this gap) · #10997 / #10998 (two more findings from the same introspection seam)

PM review of PR #11059. Flipping ready and arming auto-merge (Clause-② **no** — generated scaffold output becomes valid where it was invalid; the object-name change was measured against consumers and the dispatch's stop-condition did not fire).

## The dispatch's hardest instruction was honoured exactly

I told this seat **not** to pick a default `sharingModel` on its own judgement, because that is a security posture for every federated object this generator will ever emit. It followed #9666's resolution shape verbatim (PR #9736, live at `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`) and argued transfer rather than re-deciding.

**I doubted one link in that argument and checked it. The seat is right, and the apparent contradiction has a real explanation worth recording.**

The report claims *"'private' is what ADR-0090 D1 already resolves an unset OWD to at runtime."* My first read seemed to contradict it — `solution-blueprint.zod.ts:105` says the platform's deterministic default is *"business object → `public_read_write`"*. Those are **two different defaults at two different moments**:

- `solution-blueprint.zod.ts` is **AI authoring guidance** — what an AI should *choose* when authoring an object from a description.
- the **runtime** resolution of an unset value is `validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts:246-248`, a point-for-point mirror of `sharing-service.ts` whose own header calls it *"same fail-CLOSED default"*:

```js
if (m == null) {
  const isSystem = obj.isSystem === true || str(obj.name).startsWith('sys_');
  return isSystem ? 'public' : 'private';
}
```

A federated object is neither `isSystem` nor `sys_`-prefixed, so an unset OWD **already** resolves to `private`. And `init.ts:354` / `:420` really do emit `sharingModel: 'private'`.

⇒ Emitting it explicitly makes the existing runtime behaviour **visible** rather than changing it. **No new posture was chosen.** Recording the check because a reader hitting the blueprint line later would draw the wrong conclusion, as I briefly did.

## Both `os build` paths reported separately, which was the point of the dispatch

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `opts.primaryKey` **unset** (default) | stage 1 FAIL (missing namespace prefix) · stage 2 FAIL (`security-owd-unset`) · stage 3 PASS | **stage 1/2/3 all PASS — the draft builds end-to-end** |
| `opts.primaryKey` **set** (#11000) | fails | **still fails** — `Unrecognized key(s) on this field: primaryKey`; stage 2 never reached; `TS2353` |

⭐ And the observation that makes this report worth reading twice: **before the fix, the `primaryKey`-set path failed on `unrecognized_keys` *before* the namespace check ran — so on that path defect 1 was masked, not absent.** Error ordering was hiding a second defect. That is the kind of thing a seat only finds by measuring both paths rather than one.

Both of *this* card's defects are visibly discharged on the still-failing path too (it renders `wh_customers` and `sharingModel: 'private'`), so what remains there is **#11000's alone**. That is exactly the boundary the dispatch asked for, answered rather than blurred.

## The `src`-vs-`dist` conflict resolved — and one of the two claims turned out true-but-not-for-its-stated-reason

I handed this seat two conflicting prior claims and told it to inherit neither. It found that **both were describing different things**:

> on a fresh worktree `dist/` did NOT exist (so #11001's seat's observation reproduces) — **but it is a fact about a fresh worktree, not a property of the package**, and this worktree DOES have a `dist/` once built, so the "no dist exists" argument is unavailable and the relative-specifier argument is the one that survives

So the surviving proof is structural (`'../external-datasource-service.js'` cannot route through package `exports`), **proved empirically rather than only argued**: both ablations reddened with no rebuild between edit and run, which is only possible against `src/`.

And the `os build` harness is the opposite case, treated as such: it drives the built `dist/`, so **every** measurement through it was preceded by a build **and the fix was proved to have reached the artifact** (`marker present in 2 built files`). Two different resolution answers in one PR, each argued for its own target.

## The counter-check reached further than the assumption behind it

Sweeping `generateObjectDraft` across both repos surfaced **a route surface the card does not name** — `packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts` — which is itself the evidence that the instrument was not merely confirming what was expected. Then all 13 consumers were read individually: both route handlers pass the draft through untouched; the CLI writes `draft.source` and derives no path from the name; objectui uses it verbatim as a storage key (`metaClient.save('object', draft.name, draft.definition)` — **both halves move together**, so #7378's register contract still holds). The only two tests asserting a bare name are stubs asserting transport, not generator output.

**No consumer depends on the unprefixed name.** The stop-condition I attached did not fire, and it was tested rather than assumed.

## Two details caught by measurement, not by reasoning

- **whitespace-only namespace**: `validateObjectNamespacePrefix` skips a **falsy** namespace, but `'   '` is truthy and would have rendered `'   _customers'`. Normalised to absent and asserted. That is a bug that would have shipped.
- **absent namespace keeps the bare name and adds a loud `TODO(namespace)`** — it does **not** invent a prefix, mirroring `defineStack`, which skips the check entirely for a namespace-less stack. The dispatch warned that emitting `_customers` would trade one invalid draft for another; the seat went further and matched an existing precedent rather than picking a behaviour.

Ablations: two, one per defect, each predicting **which cases would *not* redden** as well as which would — including the double-prefix case (its table is already `wh_accounts`, so dropping the step leaves the same correct name). Both observed exactly. Restores byte-identical, both legs **re-run to a real verdict**.

`check:type-check-debt` first refused (`--re-measure cannot run: 37 workspace dependenc(ies) … no built type entry point`) — treated as NOT MEASURED, closure built exactly as `lint.yml` does (70/70), re-run to the real verdict.

## ⛔ #11061 — escalating, not ruling

`importObject`'s `opts.name` override (`const name = opts.name ?? draft.name`) is taken verbatim, and the import route forwards the request body as `opts` **unfiltered** — so `POST …/import {"name":"customers"}` persists an **unprefixed** federated object via `metadata.register('object', …)`, which applies no namespace check (`validateObjectNamespacePrefix` runs only in `defineStack()` and the publish gates). No in-tree caller exercises it today.

The seat recommends **B** (refuse an `opts.name` that fails the prefix rule, with the rule's own message) but flagged that **C's framing needs a maintainer's eye first**, and I agree — that is why I am not ruling it:

> if `register()` is meant to be gate-free **by design**, then B is the right narrow fix; if it is not, the wider hole outranks this seam.

That is a platform question about what `metadata.register('object', …)` guarantees, not a services-lane call. **B would also turn a currently-accepted request into a 4xx**, which is a contract change on top of it. Filed unassigned; needs a ruling before dispatch.

## Still open, unchanged

**#11000** remains unruled and is now measured as the *only* thing standing between the `opts.primaryKey` path and a building draft. It survived the #10676 ruling untouched (that ruling aligns the **driver** to the spec `IntrospectedColumn` contract; it does not make `fields.X.primaryKey` authorable). Flagged again for the maintainer.
